alerts.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 21 at 10:36PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
alerts.description:
The combination of hot temperatures and humidity will produce heat
index values between 108 and 111 degrees for several hours Monday
afternoon and early evening. A few locations may briefly experience
heat index values above 111 degrees.

If spending time outside on Monday, drink plenty of water, wear
light weight and light colored clothing, and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued June 22 at 2:09PM CDT until June 25 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Navasota River near Normangee affecting Grimes, Brazos and
Madison Counties.

For the Navasota River...including Normangee...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding begins as three
channels merge into one below State Highway 21. There is
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage with the river more than 1.5 miles wide. Long Trussel Road in
northeast Brazos County below State Highway 21 becomes inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM CDT Monday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 2:00 PM CDT Monday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.5
feet late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
18.5 feet on 01/16/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding begins as three
channels merge into one below State Highway 21. There is
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage with the river more than 1.5 miles wide. Long Trussel Road in
northeast Brazos County below State Highway 21 becomes inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM CDT Monday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 2:00 PM CDT Monday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.5
feet late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
18.5 feet on 01/16/2007.
